why: Populate ModCheck's standards and domain documents from its code: Program.cs and ModCheck.csproj.

ops.title: Code Style Guide
ops.description: C# code style for the ModCheck console tool: formatting, toolchain, structure and comments, with references to Program.cs
ops.body:
## Formatting
ModCheck is one file, `Program.cs`, and one project file, `ModCheck.csproj`.

- Tabs, one per level, in `Program.cs`, the same as the mod sources. The csproj uses two spaces.
- Opening brace on its own line (Allman) for the class, methods and multi-line blocks. A body of one short statement goes on the next line without braces (`if (args.Length < 2)` and the `continue` guards in `Main`).
- No line length limit. Long conditions and calls wrap after an operator or argument with the continuation indented one tab (`const BindingFlags all = ...` in `Program.cs`).
- The repository has no `.editorconfig`. TODO(owner): decide whether to add one recording tabs and brace placement for all of `common/`.

## Language and Toolchain
- C# 9 (`LangVersion` 9.0) on .NET 8 (`TargetFramework` net8.0), `OutputType` Exe. The project does not import `common/oni-mod.props`: it is a console program, not a mod, and has no game references at build time.
- ModCheck must run on .NET 8 or later, never .NET Framework. The game's interfaces use default interface methods, which the desktop CLR rejects and CoreCLR accepts, as does the game's Mono runtime. The header comment of `Program.cs` says so; keep it when the file changes.
- No NuGet packages. The code uses only `System`, `System.IO`, `System.Reflection` and `System.Runtime.CompilerServices`.

## Imports
`using` directives sit at the top, alphabetical, with no blank lines between them (`System`, `System.IO`, `System.Reflection`, `System.Runtime.CompilerServices`). No aliases and no global usings.

## Structure
- A single `internal static class Program` holds `Main` and its private static helpers (`Report`, `AllMethods`, `Unwrap`). Helpers are `private static` and sit below `Main`.
- There are no instances and no shared state: the failure and warning counters are locals of `Main` passed to `Report` by `ref`.
- A new check goes in as another loop body in `Main` or another helper beside the existing ones, and reports through `Report` so the failure and warning counts stay accurate.

## Comments
- A block comment at the top of `Program.cs` says what the tool verifies, why it needs .NET 8, and the usage line. Update it with any behaviour change.
- Comments inside the code give the reason for a rule, usually the runtime difference behind it: why `BeginInvoke` and `EndInvoke` are skipped on delegates, why the `ECall` message is a warning. No comments that restate the code.
- Console strings are plain text; the summary line uses an em dash (`runtime-mismatch artifacts, fine in-game`).

## Related
- See also: [error handling](error-handling.md)
- See also: [naming conventions](naming-conventions.md)

ops.title: Error Handling Conventions
ops.description: How ModCheck reports failures: exit codes 0, 1 and 2, the OK, FAIL and WARN output lines, per-type isolation and the ECall warning rule
ops.body:
## Principles
1. **Report every break, not the first.** A check run lists every type and method that fails, so one run shows the whole damage after a game update. `Main` counts failures and warnings and keeps going.
2. **Name the member.** Each line names the stage, the type and, for a JIT failure, the method, with the exception type and message.
3. **Tell a real break from a host artifact.** The check host is CoreCLR with no Unity engine; the game is Mono with one. Only the failures that the game would also hit count.
4. **The exit code is the verdict.** Callers (`common/tools/TestRunner/Invoke-OniTests.ps1`) read the exit code, not the text.

## Exit Codes
| Code | Meaning | Set in |
|------|---------|--------|
| 0 | every type loaded and every method compiled, warnings allowed | `Main`, `ALL CHECKS PASSED` |
| 1 | one or more failures | `Main`, `N FAILURE(S)` |
| 2 | wrong arguments, usage printed | `Main`, `args.Length < 2` |

The tool prints `usage: ModCheck <game Managed dir> <mod dll>` to standard output for exit code 2.

## Output Lines
Everything goes to standard output, one line per event, with a fixed prefix:

| Prefix | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `OK <type>` | the type stage passed (interface maps resolved, static constructor ran) and the method loop finished; `FAIL jit` lines for its methods print before it |
| `FAIL type <type>: ...` | type load, interface map or static constructor failure |
| `FAIL jit <type>.<method>: ...` | a method body could not be compiled, usually a missing method or field |
| `FAIL loader: <type> :: <message>` | one loader exception from a `ReflectionTypeLoadException` |
| `FAIL: <exception>` | any other exception while loading the assembly |
| `WARN <stage> <member>: ...` | a runtime-mismatch artifact, counted separately and not a failure |

## Handling Patterns

### Per-type isolation
The type stage and each method's JIT call are wrapped in their own `try`/`catch (Exception)` in `Main`. A failure goes to `Report`, the loop continues, and the type is not printed as `OK` when its type stage failed (`continue` after `Report`). The broad catch is the point of the tool: any exception from touching a type or method is a result to report.

### Loader exceptions
`ReflectionTypeLoadException` from `asm.GetTypes()` is caught separately and every entry of `LoaderExceptions` becomes a `FAIL loader` line and a failure. Any other exception around the whole load becomes one `FAIL:` line with the full exception text.

### Host artifacts
`Report` treats an exception whose unwrapped message contains `ECall methods must be packaged into a system module` as a warning. That message means the host tried to run Unity native code, which works in the game. `MissingMethodException`, `MissingFieldException` and `TypeLoadException` are never downgraded. `BeginInvoke` and `EndInvoke` of delegates are not compiled at all, because their stubs throw `PlatformNotSupportedException` on CoreCLR and work on Mono. Abstract methods and methods with open generic parameters are skipped.

### Unwrapping
`Unwrap` follows `TypeInitializationException` to its inner exception, so a failing static constructor shows the cause and not the wrapper.

### Assembly resolution
The `AssemblyResolve` handler looks for `<name>.dll` in the game's Managed folder and returns `null` when it is not there, which lets the runtime report the missing assembly in its own words.

## Anti-Patterns to Avoid
- Stopping at the first failure; the count and the list are the output.
- Downgrading a failure to a warning without a runtime reason written next to the rule.
- Writing results to anything but standard output and the exit code; the callers capture both.

## Related
- See also: [code style](code-style.md)

ops.title: Naming Conventions
ops.description: Naming in ModCheck: project and file names, C# member casing, the two positional arguments and the output prefixes
ops.body:
## Files and Directories
- The tool lives in `common/tools/ModCheck`: `ModCheck.csproj` and `Program.cs`. The project, the assembly and the folder share the name `ModCheck`.
- The ICON store for the tool is `common/tools/ModCheck/.context`.
- Build output goes to `bin/` and `obj/` (ignored by `common/.gitignore`).

## Code Naming
- Types, methods and parameters follow C# convention: PascalCase for types and methods (`Program`, `Report`, `AllMethods`, `Unwrap`), camelCase for parameters and locals (`managedDir`, `modDll`, `isDelegate`, `failures`).
- Local constants are camelCase too (`const BindingFlags all`).
- Methods start with a verb or name what they return: `Report`, `AllMethods`, `Unwrap`.
- Counters are plural nouns (`failures`, `warnings`) passed by `ref`.
- No `I` interfaces and no type prefixes; there is one class.

## Command Line
- Two positional arguments in a fixed order: the game's Managed directory, then the mod DLL. No options or flags.
- The mod DLL path is made absolute with `Path.GetFullPath` before use.

## Output Vocabulary
- Stages in a result line are the lowercase words `type` and `jit`; the loader failure is `loader`.
- Line prefixes are upper case: `OK`, `FAIL`, `WARN`. The final lines are `ALL CHECKS PASSED` or `<n> FAILURE(S)`.
- Types are printed by `Type.FullName`, methods by `Name` after the type, as `Namespace.Type.Method`.

## Related
- See also: [code style](code-style.md)

ops.title: ModCheck domain
ops.description: ModCheck's real things: Program and its helpers, the type-load and JIT checks, inputs, output lines, exit codes, the rules it enforces and its caller in TestRunner
ops.body:
## Overview
ModCheck loads one mod DLL against the real game assemblies on a .NET 8 host and checks, without launching the game, the two ways a mod dies after a game update: a type that cannot be set up, and a call to a member that no longer exists. It is a console program, `common/tools/ModCheck`, built and run with `dotnet run`. `common/tools/TestRunner/Invoke-OniTests.ps1` runs it on every test DLL before a game session; a mod author runs it by hand after a game update.

## Key Entities

### Program
**Description**: the whole tool: argument handling, assembly resolution, the type and method loops and the exit code.
**Location**: `Program.cs`

| Member | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `Main(string[] args)` | entry point; returns the exit code |
| `Report(stage, typeName, memberName, ex, ref failures, ref warnings)` | classifies one exception as `FAIL` or `WARN` and prints it |
| `AllMethods(type, flags)` | the type's methods and constructors in one array |
| `Unwrap(ex)` | `ExceptionType: message`, seen through `TypeInitializationException` |

**Relationships**: reads the game's Managed folder (first argument) and the mod DLL (second); writes only to standard output and the exit code.

### The two checks
1. **Type load**: for each type in the assembly, `GetInterfaceMap` for every interface of a non-interface type, then `RuntimeHelpers.RunClassConstructor`. Catches `VTable setup of type X failed` and failing static constructors.
2. **JIT**: for each non-abstract method and constructor with no open generic parameters, declared on the type (public and non-public, instance and static), `RuntimeHelpers.PrepareMethod`. Compiling the body resolves every member it references, so a missing method or field fails here instead of at call time in the game.

### Inputs
| Input | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| game Managed directory | `OxygenNotIncluded_Data\Managed` of the installed game; `Assembly-CSharp`, `0Harmony`, Unity modules and the rest resolve from here |
| mod DLL | the assembly under test; its own dependencies are resolved from the same Managed folder, so a DLL with others (TestRunner, the mod under test) is checked from a folder that holds them (see `Invoke-OniTests.ps1`) |

### Output
Lines on standard output (see [error handling](../standards/error-handling.md)) and an exit code of 0, 1 or 2.

## Business Rules
- Every type is checked even after a failure; every method of a type that loaded is checked.
- A message containing `ECall methods must be packaged into a system module` is a warning: the host cannot run Unity native code that the game runs. Everything else is a failure.
- `BeginInvoke` and `EndInvoke` of delegate types are not compiled; abstract methods and open generic methods are not compiled.
- ModCheck runs on .NET 8 or later. The desktop CLR rejects the game's default interface methods.
- A pass says nothing about behaviour at run time; it covers type setup and member resolution only.

## Domain Terminology

| Term | Definition |
|------|-----------|
| Managed directory | the folder of the game's .NET assemblies |
| JIT check | forcing compilation of a method body with `PrepareMethod` |
| Type check | touching a type's interface maps and static constructor |

## Key Code Paths

- **Whole run**: `Main` builds the resolver, loads the assembly, loops over `asm.GetTypes()` and prints the summary and exit code. See `Program.cs`.
- **One type**: the type stage in a `try`, then `AllMethods` and `PrepareMethod` per method, then `OK <type>`. See `Program.cs`.
- **Classification**: `Report` decides `FAIL` or `WARN` from the unwrapped message. See `Program.cs`.
- **Caller in the repository**: the `dotnet run -c Release --project tools\ModCheck -- <managed> <dll>` line in `common/tools/TestRunner/Invoke-OniTests.ps1`, which exits 3 when ModCheck fails.

## Related
- See also: [glossary](glossary.md)
- Governed by: [naming conventions](../standards/naming-conventions.md)

ops.title: ModCheck glossary
ops.description: Terms a newcomer to ModCheck needs: VTable setup failure, missing member, ECall, managed directory, JIT check
ops.body:
Terms a newcomer to ModCheck needs. Entity detail is in [entities](entities.md).

## Abbreviations and Acronyms

| Abbreviation | Full Term | Context |
|--------------|-----------|---------|
| ONI | Oxygen Not Included | the game whose mods ModCheck checks |
| JIT | just-in-time compiler | `PrepareMethod` forces it to compile a method before the method runs |
| CLR | Common Language Runtime | the desktop (.NET Framework) runtime that ModCheck cannot use; CoreCLR is the .NET 8 one it does use |
| ECall | external call | a method implemented in the Unity engine's native code; the host cannot run it |
| DIM | default interface method | an interface method with a body; the game's interfaces have them |

## Cross-Domain Terms

### VTable setup failure
**Definition**: the runtime error `VTable setup of type X failed` raised when a type's virtual or interface methods cannot be laid out, typically because a game interface or base class changed under the mod. `GetInterfaceMap` is how the check provokes it.
**Used in**: ModCheck output (`FAIL type ...`).

### Missing member
**Definition**: a `MissingMethodException` or `MissingFieldException`, raised when compiled code names a method or field that the game no longer has. Compiling every method body with `PrepareMethod` brings these out without calling the code.
**Used in**: ModCheck output (`FAIL jit ...`).

### Managed directory
**Definition**: the game's `OxygenNotIncluded_Data\Managed` folder, the first argument.
**Used in**: ModCheck's `AssemblyResolve` handler; `Invoke-OniTests.ps1` finds it from the game folder.

### Warning
**Definition**: a `WARN` line for an exception caused by the check host and not by the mod (the `ECall` case); it does not fail the run.
**Used in**: ModCheck output.

## Related
- See also: [entities](entities.md)
